A distinct authenticated excess can stay pending as awaiting_primary and the existing receipt worker rechecks it after primary qualification. It can establish only the excess obligation.
Reserve the original obligation. The committed claim creates the first due time. Only the winning claimant emits one bounded TLS POST to the original pin.

Persist authenticated receipt evidence before acknowledgement. Independent workers reserve the next durable due time before HTTP and use the immutable refund reference. Backoff stops growing at 900 seconds.
Qualification and repayment satisfaction commit with the open component consequence. Entitlements resolves the exact source under Privacy and Commerce acknowledges its separate commit.

security_invariants.summary: The wire uses TEST-only TLS on 127.0.0.1, the retained listener certificate, fixed fixture authorization, no redirects and no automatic retries.
Signatures authenticate raw bytes before JSON interpretation. Receipts retain normalized identifiers, bounded outcomes and a digest. They avoid raw bodies and signature headers.

Current canonical payer and immutable quote select the monetary claimant. Production has no refund mutation DSL actions, transport, ingress or fixture workers. Retained hosted payments cannot authorize a production Plan grant.

Suppress query metadata for scoped hosted Entitlements correction, refund receipt persistence and Retry-After updates. Generated AshPostgres bang queries honor the same scope. Bounded checkpoint events remain available.

concurrency.summary: Independent SQL transactions serialize admission and processed effects on the accepted purchase, then the refund row. The payment/allocation identity and the original collection limit bound owed and reserved money.
The original Plan grant and component ending take the same purchase lock. Either the grant is withheld or its exact existing right is ended.

The hosted primary exposes only the exact accepted Plan allocation. An excess payment exposes only the exact excess allocation on that distinct collection. Under the purchase lock, the payment/allocation identity and admitted sum bound all obligations, including failed and potentially sent refunds.

WELL-223 checks the exact collection under the purchase lock immediately before a first POST claim. Pending qualified-source dispute evidence or a blocking case denies a new claim. Existing claims and original owed amounts remain intact while overlap is unresolved.

idempotency_retry.summary: Exact authorization replays the same fingerprint, reference and payment. Changed input fails closed. A claim never expires into permission to POST again.
Receipts deduplicate by source, requested reference and digest. Processed financial effect belongs to one refund row and cannot be reapplied with another receipt.

A provider refund ID can bind to one claim globally. A confirmed cross-claim conflict quarantines the receipt. The existing unique index resolves a race between two first bindings. A fresh owning transaction rechecks the loser after rollback.

failure_recovery.summary: Before commit, process loss leaves the intent reserved. After a committed claim, same-reference reads continue when due. The round counter saturates at six. Backoff grows from 30 to 900 seconds. Retry-After can extend the committed due time up to 900 seconds.

A pending refund retains its next due time across process loss, discarded jobs and failed evidence inserts. A legacy unresolved round-six row with a missing due time is eligible for one fresh reservation. Only qualified processing closes read work.

The existing receipt scheduler revisits signed excess observations awaiting primary qualification. Scope mismatches and transaction identity conflicts remain quarantined. Needs-attention and failed refund outcomes preserve the exact owed amount.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: An ambiguous result cannot authorize another POST, a replacement reference or a right change. Jobs never assign money or beneficiary authority.

Ordinary charge success keeps its existing deduplication and conflict behavior. The separate charge.excess event is a TEST fixture convention. Hosted evidence cannot be presented as an E2a synthetic collection or correction.
Do not infer component attribution from current prices or amount coincidence. Keep future disputes in E2c and use the same Commerce source fence for overlap.
